Article Title: 'Taken aback by viciousness': Shashi Tharoor slams critics over Bharat Summit typo
Article Text:
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor

Tharoor's post apologising for the Bharat Summit typo

Controversy around Sonia Gandhi's memoir

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor appeared to take a swipe at the controversy over errors in Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, after drawing attention to a typo in his own social media post about the Bharat Summit. Tharoor, who had mistakenly written #BgaratSummit while sharing a video of his speech at the event, later apologised and corrected the hashtag. He subsequently shared a link to an interview and review of Sonia Gandhi's book, captioning it: "A couple of typos are being fixed online!"In a post on X, Tharoor acknowledged the error in his earlier post and said he was unable to edit it."Apologies, unable to edit the typo for some reason. Of course I meant the #BharatSummit!"The Congress MP had earlier shared a link to his full speech at the opening dinner of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on Thursday. However, the hashtag in his post appeared as #BgaratSummit instead of #BharatSummit.Soon after, Tharoor shared a separate post linking to an interview titled Sonia Gandhi, 'Belonging' And Why This Story Lies On Other Side Of Politics: my review of the book everyone is talking about. The post carried the caption, "A couple of typos are being fixed online!", in what appeared to be a reference to the discussion around errors in Sonia Gandhi's recently released memoir.Tharoor's post sharing the interview and referring to typos being fixed onlineSonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, was released in India on November 10. The book traces her childhood in post-war Italy, her relationship with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, her life in the Gandhi family and her experiences in Indian politics.The memoir has also drawn political reactions, with BJP leaders questioning several of Sonia Gandhi's accounts of key events, including the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, the Babri Masjid demolition, the Batla House encounter and the Emergency.BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan had criticised the book, saying it attempted to "whitewash" the historical wrongs of the Nehru-Gandhi family and the Congress. He also questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of her emotional responses to certain incidents and her references to the Emergency imposed by former prime minister Indira Gandhi.Tharoor's posts came amid the online discussion surrounding the memoir and his own typo in the Bharat Summit post.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor appeared to take a swipe at the controversy over errors in Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. He drew attention to a typo in his own social media post about the Bharat Summit. The Congress MP had mistakenly written #BgaratSummit while sharing a video of his speech at the event.

Article Title: Sam Pitroda, PM Modi display rare public bonhomie
Article Text:
Sam Pitroda, PM Modi display rare public bonhomie

NEW DELHI: Congress's overseas wing head, Sam Pitroda, is a vocal critic of PM Narendra Modi and the key organiser of Rahul Gandhi 's overseas outreach events.But the festive season brought out of him rare words of praise for Modi, who in turn extended his Diwali greetings to the fellow Gujarati.Modi said, "Happy Diwali and Nutan Varsh Abhinandan to you Sam Bhai and to Anjana Ben. Praying for a joyful and healthy year ahead. Jai Jagannath!"In remarks to a news agency, Pitroda had called Modi a "Gujarati friend" whom he respects as a person."My wife and I have met him. He has been very warm, kind, loving and caring at a personal level. Of course, he is a good orator and hard-working, and we get along well. We have no personal issues. I have nothing against Mr Modi as a Gujarati leader, friend or well-wisher. He has been very warm towards me, and I appreciate that. Similarly, I have been to his house in Gujarat several times," he said.Modi's greetings took even some BJP supporters by surprise. One said on X if he could wish Pitroda, he could wish him as well. Sure enough, Modi posted his Diwali greetings to him.
Article Summary: Congress's overseas wing head, Sam Pitroda, is a vocal critic of PM Narendra Modi. But the festive season brought out of him rare words of praise for Modi. Modi in turn extended his Diwali greetings to the fellow Gujarati.

Article Title: 'India showed world yoga': PM Modi praises HV Sheshadri at Bengaluru event
Article Text:
PM Modi in Bengaluru

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday praised writer and RSS leader HV Sheshadri for his contribution to nation-building, saying he dedicated his life to preparing "dedicated, capable, and disciplined citizens".Speaking at the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram at S-VYASA University in Bengaluru, PM also highlighted India's efforts to take its cultural heritage, traditional knowledge and scientific achievements to the global stage."Friends, along with the grand jubilee of Prashanti Kuttrem, this year we are celebrating the birth centenary of the revered H.V. Sheshadri. I pay my respectful homage. Sheshadri dedicated his entire life to furthering the mission of nation-building through the creation of the H.V. Seshadri Institute," PM Modi said."He knew that to take the country to the pinnacle of success it would require dedicated, capable, and disciplined citizens. Sheshadri ji devoted himself to preparing such individuals," PM Modi added.The Prime Minister also spoke about India's spiritual legacy, recalling the contribution of Swami Vivekananda in awakening the country's spiritual consciousness and introducing yoga to its youth."When the country was shackled by the chains of slavery, millions of freedom fighters were fighting for independence on one side... while on the other, there were national sages like Swami Vivekananda, who awakened India's spiritual consciousness. Showed India's youth the path of yoga. Over the past 12 years, India has confidently presented its culture, its identity, and its knowledge and science to the world. This is why the whole world now celebrates International Day of Yoga at India's initiative. Yoga asanas have also been recognized as a competitive sport in India.Events such as Khelo India and the National Games have also created new opportunities for yoga asanas. These changes are very important for India. They have also opened up opportunities for people involved. We have encouraged research related to Ayurveda and Ayurveda-based patents, and today we are seeing the results of that too. Exports of AYUSH and herbal products from India are steadily increasing," the PM said.The Golden Jubilee celebrations of Prashanti Kutiram and the birth centenary of HV Sheshadri was organised by the S-VYASA Registered Society in memory of the writer. RSS Sarkaryavah (General Secretary) Dattatreya Hosabale was the distinguished guest at the event.PM was welcomed on his arrival by Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar. Governor Sudha Yadav was also present.The Prime Minister is also scheduled to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru.Among the projects is the elevated section of Namma Metro's Pink Line, which will take the city's operational metro network beyond the 100-km mark for the first time.The corridor connecting Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere covers six stations — Kalena Agrahara, Hulimavu, IIMB (Bilekahalli-IIMB), JP Nagar 4th Phase, Jayadeva Hospital and Tavarekere.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi praised writer and RSS leader HV Sheshadri for his contribution to nation-building. PM also highlighted India's efforts to take its cultural heritage, traditional knowledge and scientific achievements to the global stage. PM is scheduled to inaugurate, dedicate to the nation, lay the foundation stone and flag off development projects worth over Rs 15,600 crore in Bengaluru.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday renewed his challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for a one-on-one public debate, claiming that the prime minister would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange.During an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram, the Congress MP was asked why he continued to insist on a public debate when the BJP had said the discussion could take place in Parliament.The leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha said he was not allowed to speak freely in the House and alleged that his microphone had been switched off."You did not let me talk on the farm bills, vote chori, SIR, China, on (Gen) Naravane's book, Epstein. I want a one-on-one debate. I don't want a debate entailing long speeches," he said.The Raebareli MP proposed a direct exchange in which both leaders could make allegations against each other, rather than deliver lengthy speeches."I want that Narendra Modi makes allegations against me and I do the same to him. He can come; there will be a table, on one side there will be Narendra Modi ji and on the other side, it would be me," he said.He added that he would have no objection if Adani Group chairperson Gautam Adani or Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat was appointed to judge the debate."But I guarantee that the prime minister will not remain the PM after a one-on-one debate with me," Rahul said.He also alleged that PM Modi is anti-national and is controlled by foreign powers.Responding to a question regarding proof of such foreign aid allegations, he said, “The proof is here. It's in this phone. The Prime Minister knows it because he taps my phone. The moment he comes for the debate, one-on-one debate, everybody will know who's controlled by foreign powers, who's an anti-national, since when he's been an anti-national, and lots of other details that I know and I wrote on my phone.”The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate. He had earlier claimed that it would take him just five minutes to establish that the prime minister was a "traitor".In a series of posts and videos shared on X last week, Rahul also challenged PM Modi to debate allegations concerning foreign influence, national security and who was anti-national.In one video, he said 24 hours had passed since he first issued the challenge and urged the prime minister to choose any venue. He proposed that the discussion take place in front of the media and the country's youth, with both leaders seated across a table and PM Modi choosing the moderator or judge. Rahul had suggested Bhagwat for the role.In another post, former Congress president renewed the challenge while responding to PM Modi's 'Dimagi Naxal' remarks. Addressing CRPF personnel who had attended the prime minister's Diwali event in Bastar, he claimed their expressions suggested they did not agree with PM Modi's comments."Your faces said it all: you didn't buy the PM's lies. He called us Naxals," Gandhi wrote.He also said the debate should address who was anti-national and who was controlled by foreign forces.BJP leaders have scoffed at Rahul's repeated calls for a debate, alleging that he has avoided discussions in Parliament.Union home minister Amit Shah has challenged Rahul to debate him in Parliament, asking him to bring his allegations and arguments to the House instead of taking political debate to the streets."If you (Rahul Gandhi) wish to engage in a responsible discussion—if your concerns hold truth, substance, and logic—then come and discuss them inside Parliament. Let’s face each other head-on! But you won’t be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away," Shah said at a rally in Karnal, Haryana.Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman has also said that Parliament already provides a platform for such an exchange and urged the Congress MP to show "some seriousness and responsibility" in his role as the leader of the opposition.Rahul's latest remarks come amid the continuing political exchange between the Congress and the BJP over his allegations against Modi and the prime minister's criticism of the opposition.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi renews his challenge to PM Modi for a one-on-one public debate. He claims PM Modi would not remain in office after facing him in a direct exchange. The Congress leader has made several public calls for PM Modi to face him in an open debate.

Article Title: Pakistan 80 years old, can't appropriate Indus Valley civilisation: Culture minister
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Friday expressed hope that Pakistan will participate in the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi from Nov 20 to 22, even as he trashed Pakistan's attempts to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, pointing out that the neighbouring nation came into existence only around 80 years ago.Fifteen countries, including China, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, have confirmed their participation for the event, which India will host at the historic Purana Quila complex. Pakistan is yet to respond to the invite. PM Narendra Modi will attend the inaugural ceremony of the dialogue forum, where India will showcase its 5,000-year-old civilisational journey.Shekhawat highlighted that PM had proposed the establishment of a Civilisational Dialogue Forum at the 2025 SCO Summit in Tianjin, and it was subsequently, welcomed and endorsed, with India announcing to host the inaugural forum.The invitation to Pakistan gains significance as it happens to be the first New Delhi has extended after Operation Sindoor last year. Ministers of 25 countries were invited, of which 15 countries have confirmed participation so far, he added.When asked about attempts by a "neighbouring country" to appropriate Indus Valley civilisation, he said if a country is trying to make such a claim, the question to ask is that "did they even exist then"."They (Pakistan) came into existence only around 80 years ago..." he said.The minister noted that Pakistan's civilisational and cultural evolution is no different from India as the former became a separate country after Partition in 1947. "So, at least on this aspect there should be no space for differences... Moreover, whatever may be a country's geopolitical, strategic and bilateral ties, one must take a step forward to reinforce cultural relations so that it can help build better dialogue and coordination between people of the two countries," he said.The minister said Purana Qila provides an appropriate setting for the forum as the archaeological excavations at the site have revealed cultural layers and evidence of early settlements dating back to approximately 1200 BCE.The four broad themes of the dialogue are civilisational and cultural expressions; art and architecture; language, literature, script and manuscript traditions; and monastic trails.
Article Summary: Fifteen countries, including China, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, have confirmed their participation for the event. Pakistan is yet to respond to the invite. PM Narendra Modi will attend the inaugural ceremony of the dialogue forum, where India will showcase its 5,000-year-old civilisational journey.

Article Title: SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad
Article Text:
SC: Indians married here can't get divorced abroad

Irretrievable breakdown of marriage no divorce ground in Indian law: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of liberal laws abroad to obtain a divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law, Supreme Court has ruled.Viewing negatively the use in a foreign court of grounds for divorce which are not recognised in India, SC said a person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist under Indian law, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.With many men approaching a foreign court to get a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage - despite the wife opposing the plea - and thereafter remarrying, SC said the person has to face proceedings even in a case where he had become a citizen of a foreign country. The top court said legal consequences stemm-ing from the subsisting marriage cannot be overridden by a subsequent change in a spouse's nationality.The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar allowed criminal proceedings for bigamy against a man who remarried after getting a divorce order from a foreign court on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage in proceedings opposed by the wife.The court said that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce in Indian law and, therefore, the divorce granted by the foreign court is not valid.“In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily. This violates the legal threshold of Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign decree has to pass through,” the SC bench said.The bench also said that if the foreign decree does not satisfy the requirements of Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, then the husband, relying on such a decree, cannot be permitted to contend that his first marriage stood dissolved in the eyes of matrimonial laws of India and, thus, escape the rigours of Section 494 of IPC (marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife).“Now, coming to the argument of the husband that since he was a British citizen when the second marriage with second wife was solemnised and since the second marriage took place outside India, keeping in view the mandate of Section 4 of the IPC, he cannot be held liable. We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as the husband was married to first wife in India under Hindu rites, rituals and customs; thus, even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the IPC cannot be said to be diluted since enquiry for the offence of bigamy cannot be confined to the place of second marriage but must necessarily take into account the subsisting matrimonial relationship. ..” the bench said.The court, however, quashed criminal proceedings against the parents and second wife of the man.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law. A person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist.

Article Title: The perils of passion
Article Text: Few stories bring together espionage, honey traps, geopolitics , artificial intelligence and infidelity like the drama unfolding around Jensen Huang , CEO of NVIDIA , the company at the heart of the AI revolution .On Nov 8, Huang wrote to NVIDIA employees and apologised to his wife, family and colleagues, admitting that he was unfaithful to his wife. The confession followed reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence officials reportedly suspected of working for Beijing.The New York Times reported on Oct 29 that Alice Huang had come under American intelligence scrutiny. The questions are unsettling. Was the world’s leading chipmaker honey-trapped? Did intimacy become a channel for information? Did a private relationship expose a company—and possibly a country—to risks no boardroom control could anticipate? This possibility alone has placed NVIDIA in an extraordinary position.Huang is not just another CEO. NVIDIA’s chips power the AI industry. Now the board must consider whether the man who built this empire has also become its greatest vulnerability. Can it remove a leader on whom the industry depends? Can it retain him without appearing to place performance above judgement? The board has announced an independent investigation. Its outcome may test corporate governance and accountability.The concept of honey traps is hardly new. In the Ramayana, the kingdom of Anga suffers drought, and the solution was to bring the young sage Rishyasringa from the forest. His visit would invoke the mercy of the rain god. King Lomapada sends beautiful courtesans to entice him. They charm the sheltered sage and lead him to the palace. The moment he enters the kingdom, the rains arrive.Stories associated with Chanakya speak of Vishakanyas—young women trained in seduction and poisoning. Sent into enemy camps, they were said to draw powerful men close and poison them, turning intimacy into a weapon. The biblical story of Samson and Delilah offers another warning: Delilah wins Samson’s trust, coaxes from him the secret of his strength and delivers him to his enemies.Men entrusted with kingdoms, institutions and secrets have surrendered judgement to desire. The tragedy is that a man may command extraordinary intelligence and still fail to recognise the danger closer to him.What must Huang be feeling today? Regret, shame, disbelief—or the hope that his stature will carry him through? How does one moment of indulgence cast a shadow over a lifetime of achievement? The personal cost is visible; the corporate and geopolitical consequences are still unfolding.Valluvar speaks of this with remarkable economy. In the chapter on Ozhukkamudaimai, he writes in Kural 136“Ozhukaththin Olgaar Uravore IzhukaththinEdham Padupakk Karindhu.”“The wise keep up the demeanour; they knowDefection is destruction.”Valluvar does not define ozhukkam—demeanour or right conduct. He goes straight to its consequences. The wise preserve their conduct because they know that a lapse is not a small departure; it can undo what they have built. Demeanour is not merely how one appears before the world. It is the discipline by which one governs oneself when temptation beckons.A man may build the future of artificial intelligence, command an industry and influence nations. Yet he remains vulnerable to an old human weakness. Sometimes the greatest threat to an empire does not stand outside its gates. It grows within.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang wrote to NVIDIA employees and apologised to his wife, family and colleagues, admitting that he was unfaithful. The confession followed reports of his relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence officials reportedly suspected of working for Beijing. NVIDIA’s chips power the AI industry.

SRINAGAR: Security forces continued Friday massive cordon and search operations to track down terrorists who shot and injured three CRPF personnel in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district two days ago.Around 200 alleged overground workers have been picked up but all have been released after questioning, a senior police officer said.CRPF chief Gyanendra Pratap Singh visited Kulgam on Friday and reviewed the situation after Wednesday’s strike that ended a long lull in attacks on security forces in the valley. Article Title: Bengaluru researchers develop chip that could help make 6G networks faster
Article Text:
Team from Bengaluru’s Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: As the world prepares for the next generation of wireless communication, researchers are working on a problem that could determine how fast future networks become: how to keep signals strong as they travel through increasingly compact devices.A team from Bengaluru’s Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) has developed a silicon chip that could help solve this problem. The chip allows high-frequency signals to pass through deliberately created barriers and sharp turns without losing much of their strength, while carrying data at speeds of up to 100 gigabits per second.The development could contribute to building smaller and more efficient circuits for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks, which are expected to use terahertz waves to transmit large amounts of data.Terahertz waves occupy a part of the electromagnetic spectrum between microwaves and infrared light. They can carry much more information than the frequencies used by today's wireless networks. But working with these waves presents a challenge. When they encounter bends, junctions or obstacles inside a circuit, some of their energy can scatter or bounce back, weakening the signal.The JNCASR team found a way to overcome this using a specially designed silicon structure.They arranged tiny triangular holes in the silicon in a pattern that allows terahertz signals to travel along a defined path. By changing the sizes of these holes over a short section, they created a barrier that the signals could cross with very little loss.In their experiments, a single barrier reduced the signal by just 1-2%, while two barriers placed one after another resulted in a loss of only 2-3%. In conventional circuits, similar obstacles can significantly weaken signals.Researchers tested the technology in three different chip designs, including one that routed signals through four sharp bends and another that split a signal into two pathways. The devices were tested at frequencies between 310 and 360 gigahertz.In data transmission experiments, one of the devices achieved speeds of 100 gigabits per second using a technique that allows information to be encoded through changes in a signal's strength and phase. At this speed, a 5GB high-definition film could theoretically be transferred in less than half a second.“Showing that terahertz waves can cross a barrier created simply by changing the hole geometry, while carrying 100 gigabits per second, suggests that this effect can become a useful design tool for terahertz chips,” said Abhishek Kumar, assistant professor at JNCASR, who led the study.The team included Samina Mulla and Sangram Kumar Sadhu as joint first authors, along with collaborators from research institutions in India, Singapore and France.An important aspect of the work is that the chip is made using high-resistivity silicon, a material compatible with established semiconductor manufacturing processes. This could make it easier to translate the research into practical devices.The findings, published in the journal Advanced Materials, could help develop compact circuits capable of directing and splitting terahertz signals on a single chip. Researchers now plan to explore ways of controlling the barriers using electrical, thermal or mechanical changes, potentially allowing signals to be redirected between different paths when required.
Article Summary: Team from Bengaluru’s Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR) has developed a silicon chip that could help solve this problem. The chip allows high-frequency signals to pass through deliberately created barriers and sharp turns.

Article Title: 'No final decision yet': Bhujbal says NCP merger talks at preliminary stage
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra minister Chhagan Bhujbal on Friday said there was no concrete decision on the proposed merger of the two NCP factions, with discussions still at a preliminary stage.The remarks came amid speculation about a possible merger between the NCP led by Sunetra Pawar and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP)."Both NCP factions coming together is a wish shared by many of us, but the question is how it can happen and who should take the initiative," Bhujbal said."There is no final decision yet. It is only discussions. We don't know what NCP (SP) wants," he added.The veteran NCP leader said any decision on the merger would require consultations with the party leadership and its allies in the BJP-led NDA. Bhujbal said the two factions had different political alignments, with one part of the BJP-led NDA and the other associated with the opposition INDIA bloc. He added that reconciling the political expectations and interests of leaders from both sides would be complicated."We (NCP) are in the government with them. We cannot take any step without consulting them. Their consent will have to be taken," he said."Everyone has their own expectations and their own perspective. How all this can be brought together is a complicated question," he said.Asked if he would take the initiative, Bhujbal said the decision rested with the party leadership."My party leaders, MLAs and district presidents will have to decide. I will express my opinion before them," he said.He also recalled a meeting at an agricultural exhibition in Baramati, where Sharad Pawar and four-five of his associates had met Ajit Pawar in the presence of Supriya Sule.However, Bhujbal said Ajit Pawar's death had altered the political situation."If Ajit Dada had been there, he would certainly have taken everyone along and led them forward. But his sudden death has changed the entire situation," he said.Sunetra Pawar, who became NCP president following her husband's death, would eventually explain the developments to party members, Bhujbal said."I am sure Sunetra tai will give everyone confidence and explain what is happening," he added.Bhujbal also spoke about his relationship with Sharad Pawar, describing him as one of Maharashtra's senior-most and most mature political leaders."Sharad Pawar's party is different and my party is different. But he is such a person that even if someone is his political enemy, he maintains relations and speaks to them. He does not bring politics into every matter," he said.
Article Summary: Mahar Maharashtra minister Chhagan Bhujbal says there is no concrete decision on the proposed merger of the two NCP factions. The remarks came amid speculation about a possible merger between the NCP led by Sunetra Pawar and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP)

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage ends after over 24 hours; Outlook, Teams restored as company says ‘underlying issue’ addressed
Article Text:
Outlook, Teams are back after more than 24 hours

Microsoft blames an earlier network upgrade for the Outlook outage

Why Outlook and Teams took almost a full day to recover

Airlines, hospitals and courts in at least 74 countries felt the Microsoft outage

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of Microsoft 365's outage affected you the most? Email communications Video conferencing File sharing 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Microsoft says the Microsoft 365 outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot for more than 24 hours is now fixed. In its final status update on the incident, the company said, “We have completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service. ” The disruption hit users in at least 74 countries and left businesses, governments, hospitals and airlines falling back on phone lines, paper records and, in some offices, fax machines.The trouble began on November 12, when users in the Americas reported they could not open their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft first acknowledged the issue at 5:54 pm GMT (11:24 pm IST). Just 13 minutes later, it warned that users in any region could be affected. The company has since said it is “deeply sorry” for the disruption and maintains the incident was not caused by a cyberattack or AI.According to a Microsoft spokesperson, the incident “was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change.” The company called it “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.”That explanation came after a long night of trial and error.Microsoft’s first updates on X blamed “elevated load” across several regions. Hours later, it said traffic had not gone up at all. A number of servers had become unexpectedly unavailable after failing automated health checks, and their workload landed on the servers still running, straining those too.Engineers eventually traced part of the problem to a core process on the affected servers that handles secure connections. It was getting overwhelmed, and the servers stopped processing requests. At one stage, Microsoft admitted its actions “have not provided the anticipated relief.”The hardest part was keeping servers up once they were back. Microsoft said servers it returned to service could stop responding again once they started receiving traffic. Its engineers worked on several fronts at once. They limited the types of traffic hitting affected infrastructure, rolled some servers back to an earlier configuration, patched an authentication and routing component and added virtual machines for extra capacity.Email made the job slower. Mail servers outside Microsoft keep retrying messages they could not deliver, so restored servers faced a backlog of queued mail the moment they came online. To make sure messages sent during the outage were not lost, Microsoft extended its email timeout window to 48 hours.“Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration,” the company said.Asia Pacific was among the first regions to stabilise on November 13, followed by Europe and North America. By the afternoon of November 13 (GMT), Microsoft said email queues were “significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.” Teams chats and meetings had largely come back earlier, though calendar features that rely on Exchange Online stayed patchy for longer. Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote and Microsoft To Do, used on personal accounts, were hit as well.Microsoft said in January it had more than 450 million paid commercial subscriptions to its 365 services. That reach showed in who got hit.In India, the outage hit email support at IndiGo and Akasa Air. Air India rerouted its emails to keep receiving customer messages, and its flights ran as usual. At one large Indian brokerage, a backup covered for Outlook, but client calls on Teams were harder to manage.In the UK, NHS staff switched to paper records, pharmacies warned of prescription delays and a judge in Manchester sent jurors home. In Colorado, a sheriff’s office had to ask people to post bond in person, since online payments relied on Outlook email notifications. Some companies in Japan went back to fax. Even OpenAI and Anthropic ran into problems with their Microsoft 365 connectors, while electric truck maker Workhorse Group pushed its quarterly results to November 16.Investors were far calmer. Microsoft shares traded largely flat on November 13, even as the outage stretched into a second day.For users, a few loose ends may remain. Emails held in queues carry the time they were delivered rather than sent, so a message stamped November 13 may well have been written on the night of November 12.Microsoft has promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete. That report should spell out how a capacity upgrade knocked servers offline across regions for more than a day, and what the company is changing so the next network update does not do the same.
Article Summary: Microsoft blames an earlier network upgrade for the Outlook outage. The disruption hit users in at least 74 countries and left businesses, governments, hospitals and airlines falling back on phone lines, paper records and, in some offices, fax machines. Outlook, OneDrive, OneNote and Microsoft To Do, used on personal accounts, were hit as well.

Article Title: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry confronts critic over controversial motherhood remarks as Stephen Curry’s family finds itself back in the spotlight
Article Text:
Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry slams critics. Image via: Getty Images

Why did Ayesha Curry respond to a critic over her motherhood remarks?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Curry’s Instagram message to Arenas and Young

Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry replied to an online critic on Friday after an old podcast clip of hers went viral. The video, reposted Wednesday night, features her saying she once did not want kids or marriage. One X user called her comments disturbing and accused her of complaining about motherhood. Ayesha answered with a short, direct post. She says she was only answering a question about her childhood plans. The exchange comes days after the Warriors superstar defended her over a Roku movie role and remarks from former NBA players.The clip comes from Ayesha’s 2025 appearance on the Call Her Daddy podcast. She described herself back then as a career-focused woman who did not want kids, did not want to marry and never dreamed about wearing a wedding dress. Stephen Curry’s wife was describing her younger self, not her feelings about parenting now.When the video resurfaced, an X user wrote a long reply. The post called her remarks disturbing and said a husband, children and the chance to be present while raising them are blessings many women pray for. It also said motherhood takes sacrifice, but children are not why anyone misses out on life."Watching Ayesha Curry complain about motherhood is disturbing.Having a husband, beautiful children and the opportunity to be present while raising them are blessings so many women pray for," the user commented on the post.The user further added to the controversy, “Motherhood requires sacrifice. We all know that. But your children are not the reason you missed out on life… Imagine being so focused on what you think motherhood took from you that you fail to appreciate everything God has given you… And here you are complaining about the very blessings they are begging God for.”Ayesha saw it Friday morning and answered. “I’ve never complained a day in my life,” she wrote. She said the question she had been asked was about what she pictured for herself as a little girl. Her point was simple. A comment about an old mindset had been read as a present-day complaint. She did not argue about parenting or defend her choices. She corrected the framing and left it there.Her role in the Roku rom-com Second Chance Holiday set off the earlier round of talk. Gilbert Arenas called Ayesha “the only blemish” on an otherwise spotless family image and compared her with other NBA stars’ wives. Nick Young also weighed in.Curry answered on Wednesday in an Instagram message that named Nick Young, Arenas and Emmanuel. He said they were offering opinions on something they did not know about, and that it spoke to a bigger conversation about how women are viewed and what they are allowed to do. He cited ignorance about how acting works. The Warriors superstar first tried to laugh it off, he said, but “something needs to be said.”He asked them to offer congratulations on the movie, and said any apology should be as loud as the shows that led with the topic. He ended by thanking the podcasters for promoting the film and urging them to show his wife more respect.
Article Summary: Stephen Curry’s wife Ayesha Curry replied to an online critic on Friday after an old podcast clip of hers went viral. The video, reposted Wednesday night, features her saying she once did not want kids or marriage. One X user called her comments disturbing and accused her of complaining about motherhood. She says she was only answering a question about her childhood plans.

Article Title: “The truth didn’t save me..”: Mike Tomlin revisits $100,000 NFL fine after controversial Jacoby Jones incident against Baltimore Ravens in 2013
Article Text:
Mike Tomlin revisits $100,000 NFL fine

Mike Tomlin explains why he moved into Jacoby Jones’ path during the 2013 Ravens game

NFL handed Tomlin a $100,000 fine despite his explanation, while Ben Roethlisberger defended him

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mike Tomlin still remembers the night his actions became one of the biggest talking points of a Steelers-Ravens game. On December 2, 2013, the Pittsburgh Steelers coach found himself at the center of a controversy involving Baltimore returner Jacoby Jones. The NFL later fined Tomlin $100,000, but he has always maintained that he never tried to interfere with Jones’ kickoff return.After years, Tomlin has offered a closer look at what happened that night. Speaking on the Not Just Football podcast, the Steelers coach explained how watching the stadium's jumbotron left him disoriented and why he moved just before Jones reached the sideline.The incident happened in the third quarter after Pittsburgh scored a touchdown against Baltimore. Jacoby Jones caught the ensuing kickoff and began a long return. As he ran down the sideline, he came dangerously close to Tomlin, who stood near the playing area.The return covered 73 yards, but the attention quickly shifted to the Steelers coach. Television replays showed Tomlin smiling on the jumbotron, adding to the suspicion that he might have deliberately stepped into Jones' path to slow him down.Tomlin offered a different explanation on the Not Just Football podcast.He said he had been watching the kickoff through the stadium screen when he suddenly noticed himself appearing on it."The truth didn't save me from a fine," Tomlin said on the podcast. "I got fined a hundred thousand dollars after the ball was kicked."He also explained that the screen gave him a confusing view of the play."Spatially, I get disoriented where I am and I'm watching something that I don't want to happen," Tomlin recalled. He said he immediately moved to his left after spotting himself on the jumbotron because he feared Jones might run straight into him.His explanation also came down to a routine he followed during kickoff returns.Tomlin told the podcast that he regularly spoke to his kickoff team before they took the field. He would then stand near the yard line where the ball was kicked from to check whether his players were onside. Once the kick happened, he usually watched the play on the stadium screen because it offered an aerial view.However, Baltimore's stadium had only one jumbotron at the time. That made it harder for Tomlin to judge his position while following the return.The NFL did not accept the incident as an innocent mistake. After reviewing the footage and investigating Tomlin's actions, the league fined him $100,000 for standing too close to the field and interfering with the return.The league believed Tomlin had stepped onto the playing field. Officials considered his actions serious enough to warrant an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty.The Steelers also received a warning that the league could take away draft picks in the 2014 NFL Draft. However, Pittsburgh did not lose any selections.Jones also spoke about the incident after the game. The Ravens returner admitted that Tomlin's presence affected his run, although he took responsibility for not finishing the play."It broke my stride a little bit," Jones said after the game. "(But) I still shouldn't have got caught."Tomlin did receive support from his own quarterback. Ben Roethlisberger defended the coach during a 2013 appearance on 93.7 The Fan, saying he did not believe the move was intentional."I don't think it was intentional," Roethlisberger said. He also explained that he understood why Tomlin watched the jumbotron, as it offered a better view of the action.Interestingly, the controversy did not prevent Tomlin from bringing Jones to Pittsburgh later. In November 2015, the Steelers claimed the wide receiver off waivers.The incident remains a memorable moment from Tomlin's coaching career. More than a decade later, his explanation makes clear that he still disputes the idea that he tried to disrupt Jones' return. The $100,000 fine, however, remains part of the story.
Article Summary: Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin was fined $100,000 by the NFL for interfering with a kickoff return. Tomlin said he was watching the kickoff through the stadium screen when he suddenly noticed himself appearing on it. He said he immediately moved to his left after spotting himself on the jumbotron.

Article Title: Sophie Cunningham Eyes New Contract After Admitting Frustration With Her Game Ahead Of Major 2027 Transformation
Article Text:
Sophie Cunningham. Image via: Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images

Why is Sophie Cunningham not satisfied with her game?

Cunningham heads into free agency without Amber Cox

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham says she is not satisfied with her game and plans to spend the offseason changing it. The 30-year-old Fever guard said so on No Hesitation, the podcast she co-hosts with Drew Hanlen. Free agency opens January 30. Cunningham’s one-year deal is about to run out, and Indiana is bringing in a new front office after an early playoff exit. She led all bench players with 7.9 points a game and shot 42% from three this season, yet the spot-up shooter label no longer fits what she wants to become.Since arriving in a 2025 trade, Cunningham has been viewed as a floor spacer who can catch and shoot at any moment, a spark off the bench when a three is needed. This season’s scoring was a slight dip from the 8.6 points and 43% from three she posted in 2025, but it was a solid return from an MCL tear.The point came up while Cunningham and Hanlen, an NBA and WNBA trainer, went through some defensive plays on the podcast. She said the level was below standard.“I’m not satisfied with where I’m at,” Cunningham said.She says she has far more to give and wants help from people like Hanlen spotting what she is missing and what she is already doing.The offseason, she said, is the time to expand, and she expects it to be a great one, with the goal of becoming a more complete player.Indiana’s season ended in late September with a first-round loss to the Las Vegas Aces. Indiana now has a full offseason to sort out. Amber Cox, the former general manager, made that trade. Cox is gone, so Cunningham has lost the front-office ally who made the deal, and the Fever plan to hire a new group.As an unrestricted free agent, Cunningham has no guarantee of a return for the 2027 WNBA season.The offseason has been busy away from the court. Cunningham has turned up at NASCAR events and promoted the brands she works with. She also sat down with Theo Von for his This Past Weekend show, a taping she says ran three hours or more before being trimmed to under two. Asked about the missing hours of footage, she joked it “didn’t air for a reason.” She called Von hilarious with a good heart and said the cut material was funny.Cunningham is also slated to take part in Project B, a new basketball league that tips off in January, the same month free agency opens.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham says she is not satisfied with her game and plans to spend the offseason changing it. Cunningham’s one-year deal is about to run out, and Indiana is bringing in a new front office after an early playoff exit. Cunningham led all bench players with 7.9 points a game and shot 42% from three this season.

Article Title: In 1985, Willie Nelson joined two musicians to launch Farm Aid as US family farms struggled; 41 years later, the annual concerts and wider campaign have raised over $90 million to support farmers and
Article Text:
Willie Nelson Photo: Farm Aid / Instagram

How Farm Aid began

The musicians behind the mission

What the 2026 concert achieved

Food, farming and community

More than a concert

A legacy still growing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In 1985, Willie Nelson joined fellow musicians Neil Young and John Mellencamp to launch Farm Aid at a moment when family farms across the United States were under severe financial pressure. Four decades later, the annual concert has become one of the country’s most recognisable examples of musicians turning a stage into a platform for social change. According to Farm Aid, the organisation has raised more than $90 million since 1985 to support programs that help farmers thrive, expand access to food from family farms, and challenge the dominance of industrial agriculture.The 2026 festival showed that the mission remains far more than nostalgia. Held in Virginia Beach, the event brought together 14,000 attendees from every US state, Puerto Rico, the Virgin Islands, five Canadian provinces and 19 countries. It also reached millions more through television and online broadcasts, with Farm Aid reporting 8.05 million CNN viewers and more than 3.1 million people watching its YouTube livestream.Farm Aid was created in response to the farm crisis of the 1980s, when falling prices, rising debt and broader economic upheaval left many family farmers struggling to hold on to their land. Nelson, Young and Mellencamp organised the first concert to raise money and public attention for farmers whose livelihoods were being threatened.From the beginning, the idea was not simply to write cheques. Farm Aid positioned itself as an advocate for family-scale agriculture, arguing that the people who grow food should have a viable place in the American economy. The organisation’s stated work includes helping farmers thrive, expanding the reach of what it calls the Good Food Movement, and promoting food from family farms.That combination of music, fundraising and advocacy has proved durable. More than 40 years after the first show, Farm Aid continues to stage an annual festival and to use the attention around it to connect consumers, policymakers and farmers.Willie Nelson, Neil Young, John Mellencamp, Dave Matthews, Margo Price and Nathaniel Rateliff serve as Farm Aid artists and board members, hosting the annual festival. Their involvement has helped keep the cause visible across generations of music fans, while the artists themselves donate their performances each year.The 2026 event featured 18 artists who performed without payment in support of family farmers. That model remains central to Farm Aid’s identity: the concert is not merely a benefit show with famous names attached, but a recurring gathering of performers who lend their time and cultural influence to a long-running campaign.The festival also creates space for farmers to speak for themselves. Before the music began, seven Virginia farmers joined artists on stage for a press event, sharing their experiences and visions for agriculture. Five farmers were also heard on the FarmYard stage, where they discussed pressing issues and shared stories about food and farming in their region and across the country.The 2026 festival was attended by 14,000 people, but its reach extended well beyond the venue. Farm Aid reported 8.05 million viewers across CNN’s global platforms, more than 3.1 million YouTube livestream viewers, and 194 virtual watch parties across 31 states.The event generated 3,300 news stories, with coverage from outlets including Billboard and Rolling Stone. That attention matters because Farm Aid’s work depends not only on donations but on keeping the pressures facing family farmers in the public conversation.The festival also had a local impact. With help from Support+Feed, attendees donated 10,000 pounds of nonperishable food to the Foodbank of Southeastern Virginia and the Eastern Shore. Volunteers from 33 states helped run the event, while 426 farmers and advocates took part in pre-festival events, trainings and farm tours.Farm Aid’s 2026 festival made a deliberate effort to connect concertgoers with the people and products behind their food. Its HOMEGROWN Concessions program featured 71 items sourced from local farms, co-ops, food hubs and small businesses, including Virginia peanuts, Chesapeake poutine with hand-picked blue crab, and local cheeses.Six Virginia farmers supplied thousands of flowers, hundreds of corn shocks, pumpkins, gourds and hay bales for the venue’s decorations, along with a tractor. The HOMEGROWN Youthmarket gave young people from FFA, 4-H and Petersburg Is Growing the chance to share fresh produce and baked goods while explaining their work in local communities.There were also 45 HOMEGROWN Village exhibitors, offering hands-on activities about soil, water, energy and food. Demonstrations covered restoring soil with cover crops, making salsa, processing wool and growing mushrooms at home, while a seed swap gave attendees a practical way to participate in the ideas being discussed.Farm Aid describes its mission as broader than raising money for individual farmers. The organisation says its work aims to expand the reach of the Good Food Movement, take action to change the dominant system of industrial agriculture, and promote food from family farms.The 2026 event reflected that wider ambition. Twelve policymakers from Virginia spoke with farmers, learned about their challenges and discussed ways to support family farm agriculture. The festival also brought together artists, farmers and advocates for conversations about land, family and legacy, rather than treating farmers only as beneficiaries of charity.Even the environmental details carried the message. Working with Tidewater Compost, Farm Aid diverted more than 12,000 pounds of organic material from landfills to support future crops in Virginia.More than 41 years after Willie Nelson, Neil Young and John Mellencamp launched Farm Aid, the organisation has raised more than $90 million. The figure represents decades of concerts, donated performances, volunteer labour and public support for a cause that began during a national farm crisis.The 2026 numbers suggest that the model still resonates. Thousands attended in person, millions watched remotely, and the festival generated both money and attention for family farmers.Farm Aid’s lasting achievement may be less about any single dollar amount than about its persistence. What began in 1985 as an urgent response to farmers in trouble has become an annual institution that continues to connect music fans with the people who grow the country’s food.
Article Summary: Willie Nelson, Neil Young and John Mellencamp launched Farm Aid in 1985. The organisation has raised more than $90 million since then. The 2026 festival in Virginia Beach was attended by 14,000 people. The event was watched by 8.05 million people on CNN and 3.1 million on YouTube.

Article Title: 'Harassed in name of love': 17-year-old cricketer, who played BCCI U-15 trophy, dies by suicide in Telangana; kin blames 2 youths
Article Text:
A 17-year-old girl was found dead at her grandmother's house in Vikarabad on Friday.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





HYDERABAD: Promising cricketing career of a 17-year-old girl came to a tragic end after she was found dead at her grandmother's house in Vikarabad on Friday, with her family alleging that harassment by two youths drove her to take the extreme step.The incident sparked protests in the town, with her relatives blocking a road and demanding the immediate arrest of the two accused. Vikarabad town inspector Raghu Kumar told TOI that the girl had been undergoing cricket coaching in Vikarabad. She had represented in the BCCI Under-15 One-Day Trophy during the 2023-24 season."She was playing in local cricket matches but had not been selected for the BCCI Under-19 team yet. She completed her open Intermediate course this year in Pargi, where she came into contact with two persons. One of them allegedly harassed her in the name of love," he said.She had been staying at her grandmother's house in Vikarabad while pursuing her studies and undergoing specialised cricket coaching for Under-19 tournaments, police said.According to the family, she had been facing harassment allegedly from two youths over the past few days.The family alleged that one of them had been pursuing her in the name of love, while the other youngster was also troubling her. The family suspects that their harassment may have driven her to take the extreme step. No suicide note was found. The inspector said police seized the budding cricketer's mobile phone and were examining its contents to establish the circumstances leading to her death.A case of suspicious death has been registered and further investigation is under way.Meanwhile, family members and relatives staged a road blockade in Vikarabad, demanding the arrest of the two youths accused of harassing her. They threatened to continue the protest until action was taken against those responsible. The blockade disrupted traffic and created tension in the town.
Article Summary: A 17-year-old girl was found dead at her grandmother's house in Vikarabad on Friday. Her family alleges that harassment by two youths drove her to take the extreme step. Incident sparked protests in the town, with her relatives blocking a road and demanding the immediate arrest of the two accused.

Article Title: 'CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Starc or Lyon': David Warner makes fresh bombshell claim on ball-tampering, accuses Cricket Australia of 'cover up'
Article Text:
Photo/screengrab

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Australia opener David Warner has accused Cricket Australia (CA) of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, questioning the governing body's investigation into the incident.In another development in the controversy that rocked Australian cricket, Warner claimed that CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon during its investigation in the days after the Cape Town Test in 2018.Warner made the allegation in an Instagram post on Saturday, a day after accusing Test captain Pat Cummins of throwing Usman Khawaja under the bus following the release of Khawaja's memoir, Sabr.His latest comments came a day after Cummins addressed the allegations made in Khawaja's book during a lengthy press conference. The Australia captain dismissed the claims as “complete and utter nonsense”.“As far as I am aware, CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon in their 2018 investigation,” Warner posted to Instagram.“If that’s correct, then how can CA push the idea that the bowlers didn’t know?“It looks like they had decided who they wanted to blame from the very beginning ran a shoddy investigation to serve the purpose and now they want to maintain the false narrative that the bowlers had no idea.That stinks of a cover up.”The ball-tampering scandal has returned to the spotlight after Khawaja made several claims while promoting his book, alleging that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the Cape Town Test.Cummins rejected those claims on Friday, while CA has previously said it has no intention of reopening the investigation into the incident.Warner had also responded to Cummins' comments on Friday afternoon, ahead of Australia's opening ODI of the summer against England. He said he felt "the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus".The former Australia opener followed that up with another Instagram post on Saturday, questioning the way CA handled the investigation.Warner and then captain Steve Smith were handed one-year bans by CA following the incident, while Cameron Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.
Article Summary: Former Australia opener David Warner has accused Cricket Australia of covering up details of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal. Warner claimed that CA did not interview Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc or Nathan Lyon during its investigation in the days after the Cape Town Test in 2018. His latest comments came a day after Test captain Pat Cummins addressed the allegations made in Usman Khawaja's book.

Article Title: Stephen Curry's defense of Ayesha gets Stephen A. Smith's heartfelt praise following kissing scene debate
Article Text:
Stephen Curry. Image via: Kelley L Cox - Imagn Images

What did Stephen Curry say about the criticism of Ayesha?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Smith wants the Warriors to lean on Yaxel Lendeborg without Curry

Stephen A. Smith has praised Stephen Curry for his response to criticism aimed at Ayesha Curry . Gilbert Arenas and Emmanuel Acho had both brought up a clip from her Roku project, Second Chance Holiday, in which she kisses a male actor, and criticized her over it. Curry answered with a pointed but polite statement, and Arenas, Acho and Nick Young have all apologized since. Smith took the topic to his own show to speak about Curry’s character, not the clip. The Warriors superstar is also missing time with an oblique tear.Curry’s message was polite and pointed. Anytime Ayesha shows up in a headline, the Warriors guard suggested, people should offer “the happy hands, the congratulations” and make any apology as loud as the coverage was. Curry then thanked everyone for the free promotion and pointed viewers to Second Chance Holiday on Roku, where Ayesha stars.Smith zeroed in on the tone. Even when Curry is calling people out, he said, the guard stays nice about it. Arenas, Young and Acho got credit for apologizing. The reason for bringing it up at all, Smith explained, was to shine a light on Curry. Smith’s verdict: “Just one of the most decent brothers you’ll ever meet in your life.”Smith also said anyone with something negative to say about a person close to Curry should stop and think first.The praise arrives while Golden State adjusts to life without its star. An MRI confirmed an oblique tear for Curry, and Smith has a view on who should pick up the slack. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg is his answer. Smith said he loves the kid and is a big fan of what Lendeborg brings.Smith was careful about expectations. “Nobody is Steph Curry,” he said. Still, he thinks the rookie can be given the ball more often and lead a more active offense for the team.Draymond Green is part of the same plan. Smith wants Green to be more efficient and aggressive on offense, though not to an extreme. Three points a game is too low, Smith agreed. Ten or 11 is about Green’s range, and if Green is also playmaking and defending, that works for Smith. ESPN’s Kendrick Perkins argues Green is the player who has to step up.Golden State is 8-4 and sixth in the West, ahead of Oklahoma City and Memphis and behind Portland and Houston. San Antonio was next, in an NBA Cup game on Friday.
Article Summary: Stephen A. Smith praised Stephen Curry for his response to criticism aimed at Ayesha Curry. Gilbert Arenas and Emmanuel Acho had both brought up a clip from her Roku project, Second Chance Holiday, in which she kisses a male actor. Curry answered with a pointed but polite statement, and Arenas, Acho and Nick Young have all apologized.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Saturday became the youngest captain in men's T20 cricket history when he led Bihar in their opening match of the 2026-27 Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy against Saurashtra at the Holkar Stadium in Indore.At 15 years and 232 days, Sooryavanshi broke the record previously held by Croatia's Zach Vukusic, who captained his national side in a T20 International at the age of 17 years and 311 days last year. Although he has been named Bihar captain for the first two matches of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he is likely to join the India A squad for the Rising Stars Asia Cup in Qatar, which begins on November 19.The 15-year-old already holds two other records in T20 cricket. Article Title: A 101-year-old US veteran who earned two Purple Hearts during World War II says his wife helped him rebuild his life; Joseph Allegretti has now recalled their nearly 72-year marriage in a new Veterans
Article Text:
Joe and Janet Allegretti in an undated picture (AI refined)Photo credit: Joe Allegretti/ PEOPLE

The war he cannot forget

Representative image of a depressed man from Canva

Coming home changed

Janet became his light

A life beyond the battlefield

Life after Janet

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What Veterans Day means to him

Joseph “Joe” Allegretti, a 101-year-old World War II veteran who earned two Purple Hearts, says the person who helped him most after the war was not a commander, a medic, or a fellow soldier. It was Janet Kajano, the woman he married in 1949 and shared nearly 72 years with before her death in 2021. In a new Veterans Day interview with PEOPLE, Allegretti reflected on the war that shaped him, the marriage that steadied him, and the life he built after returning home to Albany, New York.Allegretti is among the small number of combat infantrymen from World War II still alive at 101. He served from August 1943 until his discharge in January 1946, earning two Purple Hearts, a Bronze Star, the Combat Infantryman’s Badge, and France’s Legion of Honour. Yet when he speaks about his life now, his thoughts return again and again to Janet, whom he called his “new guiding light.”Allegretti was born on May 17, 1925, and grew up in Albany during the Great Depression. His parents separated when he was 10, and he has described those years as a daily challenge, with enough food but few extras. His mother, Florence, became a central source of support, and he remembers her as the “shining light” of his childhood.He graduated from Albany’s Christian Brothers Academy in June 1943 and was drafted into the Army that August, at age 18. After basic training, he joined the 104th Infantry Division, known as the Timberwolves, the first American division trained for night fighting.At 19, Allegretti was part of the Allied advance into Inden, Germany, in December 1944. He and his lieutenant were caught in a surprise German ambush, and shrapnel struck Allegretti in his left thigh after enemy soldiers threw grenades as the two men tried to move past them. He was eventually airlifted to Birmingham, England, to recover.The injuries did not end there. Two months later, while his division tried to cross the Roer River in rowboats, enemy fire capsized the boats and Allegretti nearly drowned in the current. In March 1945, German tanks blew him into the air, leaving him with a brain concussion.When Allegretti returned to Albany in 1946, he carried more than medals and memories. He had survived combat, but he also carried the emotional weight of what he had seen and done. “I left the war, but the war never left me,” he told People.He has said that combat remains difficult to discuss, especially with people who did not experience it. “Soldiers who were involved in close combat with the enemy can be reluctant to discuss their actions with anyone other than fellow combat veterans,” he explained. “I keep it to myself.”Years ago, he spoke with a priest about the uncertainty that haunted him, including whether people who died in battle had been killed by his own weapon. The priest told him it had been a “just war,” an answer that Allegretti has carried with him.After returning home, Allegretti enrolled at Siena College and married Janet Kajano in 1949. He has been direct about the effect she had on him. “The war messed my mind up. Janet became my new guiding light,” he told PEOPLE.Their marriage lasted nearly 72 years, until Janet died in 2021 at age 96. Together they raised four children, Joe, Lucille, Patti and Jim, and became grandparents to five and great-grandparents to nine.Allegretti said he tried to be more than a father to his children. He wanted to be a friend and mentor, someone they could speak with openly and trust to listen with understanding and respect. That approach reflected the family life he had wanted to create after growing up as an only child whose parents had separated.With help from his father, he bought the only house he has ever owned in 1957. He and Janet filled it with family life, travel plans, volunteer work, and routines that stretched across decades.Allegretti worked for 27 years at the New York State Thruway Authority, retiring in 1986 as its director of accounting. After retirement, he and Janet enjoyed trips to Italy and the Jersey Shore, along with visits to their timeshare in Aruba, where they walked for miles along white-sand beaches at sunset.They also spent time at Albany’s Italian American Community Center and the city’s Irish Hall, and they volunteered in their community. Their family later grew into a wider circle that includes Danny Freeman, one of their grandchildren, a lawyer turned TikTok creator known as @dannylovespasta, who wrote two bestselling cookbooks inspired by Janet’s Italian recipes.Allegretti credits part of his longevity to habits formed during his marriage. He says he has followed a Mediterranean diet since he and Janet married, and after retiring he spent 31 years going to the gym three times a week for two hours at a time.Janet’s death changed the shape of Allegretti’s daily life. He says he misses everything about her, including her warm smile and fun spirit, and he has acknowledged that the sparkle in his life dimmed after she was gone.In July, he suffered an unexpected fall in his own kitchen, leading to hospitalisation. Realising he could no longer live alone, he decided to sell the house he had owned for 69 years and moved in with his son Joe and daughter-in-law Suzanne just outside Albany.He began weekly at-home hospice visits in August, but he remains engaged with the world around him. He studies the stock market, follows the news, reads thrillers and mysteries, and has finally completed a novel about a wartime love story that he began years earlier.He hopes it may be published after his death.As he marked his 80th Veterans Day, Allegretti said he wishes people paid closer attention to veterans, particularly those who experienced combat. “The many sharp and deep emotions have taken their toll on combat veterans,” he told People. “World War II is still being fought in the dreams of many of us today.”His story is not only one of wartime bravery. It is also a story about what can come after survival: a long marriage, a family, steady work, community involvement, and the quiet work of carrying memories that never fully disappear.Allegretti still finds reasons to look forward. “There is still more joy in life,” he said, repeating a lesson Janet often shared: “It is what it is. It could be worse.”
Article Summary: Joseph 'Joe' Allegretti, 101, served in World War II and earned two Purple Hearts. He married Janet Kajano in 1949 and the couple had four children. Janet died in 2021 at age 96, and he is now grandparents to five and great- grandparents to nine.
